newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: WTO chief hopes for swift end to EU-US trade row.
newsitem.headline: WTO chief hopes for swift end to EU-US trade row.

text.p: The Director-General of the World Trade Organisation said on Tuesday he hoped the European Union and the United States soon solved the row that has erupted over the controversial Helms-Burton Act.
"I hope this question will be solved by bi-lateral agreement but I'm not going to make any further comment," Renato Ruggiero of the Geneva-based body told a press conference.

The European Union agreed on Monday to make it illegal for Europeans to obey the U.S. anti-Cuba trade law, which allows naturalised Americans to sue in U.S. courts foreign companies or individuals deemed to have gained from investments in property confiscated in Cuba since the communist revolution of 1959.
The EU law will prohibit Europeans from complying with the act and allow them to reclaim damages in EU courts.

Ruggiero was visiting the Dutch employers' federation on the invitiation of the government, which said it would propose a system of zero tariffs on goods from least developed nations at the WTO meeting in December.
Dutch trade minister Anneke van Dok said the issue was one of her government's top priorities as it prepared its schedule for the meeting to be held in Singapore.

"This proposal is a consequence of the discussions we had in the former round (of negotiations)," she said. "It is a proposal for which I have support from within the European Union but whether or not we get it from outside...."
Ruggiero said he personally supported the Dutch proposal.
"There is full support from my side. There is perfect harmony between the Dutch government and the WTO on this...at least the WTO secretariat," he said.
